title: Acceleration and Motion Graphs

standard_text: Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity; uniform acceleration; distance–time and velocity–time graphs describe motion; the gradient of a velocity–time graph is acceleration and the area under it is displacement. (summary of the Intermediate Science curriculum, JSS 2, theme: You and Energy)
meta_desc: Free JSS 2 Intermediate Science worksheets (NERDC curriculum, theme: You and Energy): acceleration, velocity–time graphs, distance–time graphs, free fall and equations of motion. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: The gradient of a velocity–time graph is the acceleration.
body_html:
How to think about it

Acceleration is how quickly velocity changes: a = (v − u)/t, measured in m/s². An object speeding up has a positive acceleration; one slowing down has a negative acceleration (deceleration).

On a distance–time graph, a straight sloping line shows constant speed and a curve shows changing speed. On a velocity–time graph, the gradient is the acceleration and the area under the line is the displacement.

Example

0 to 20 m/s in 5 s. Acceleration?

(20 − 0)/5

Answer: 4 m/s²

Example

A horizontal line on a velocity–time graph means?

Velocity not changing

Answer: constant velocity (zero acceleration)

Common mistakes

  • Reading a distance–time graph as a velocity–time graph.
  • Thinking a negative acceleration always means moving backward.
  • Forgetting units of m/s².

items.q: A car slows down from 11.5 m/s to rest in 3 s. What is its acceleration?
items.e: a = (0 − 11.5) ÷ 3 = −3.833333 m/s². The minus sign means it is slowing down (deceleration).
